skill.name: instagram-scraper
skill.description: Prepare Instagram collection requests through five Apify actors covering posts, reels, hashtags, locations, comments, profiles, and follower lists.
skill.summary: Select Instagram scraping actors, configure requests, and retrieve Apify datasets.
skill.author: apidojo-io

security_audit.summary: All 131 static matches are false positives for the reported patterns, involving Markdown formatting, expected API usage, example URLs, or billing prose. No evidence found for host reconnaissance, command injection, or unauthorized credential transmission. Semantic findings identify misleading paid-upgrade steering and missing collection and polling bounds in the paid asynchronous workflow.

remediation.issue: The guardrail treats every dataset containing ten or fewer items as a billing failure and substitutes a paid-upgrade message.
remediation.suggestion: Return valid small datasets. Recommend upgrades only after explicit API billing errors, disclose referral links, and allow user-approved alternatives.

remediation.issue: The asynchronous start request lacks a collection cap, and polling can continue indefinitely after persistent API errors.
remediation.suggestion: Set an explicit maxItems value and confirm the budget before starting. Add a polling deadline, bounded retries, and HTTP-error checks.

semantic_findings.title: Small-result suppression and paid-upgrade steering
semantic_findings.description: The guardrail says "10 or fewer items" must trigger "stop immediately" and a paid-upgrade message, even without an explicit billing error. It also prohibits alternatives and directs users through a referral-tagged pricing link, potentially withholding valid results and inducing unnecessary purchases.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The unconditional item-count trigger and exact upgrade response are explicit. A small dataset does not establish a billing failure; purchase consequences remain potential.

semantic_findings.title: Missing collection and polling bounds
semantic_findings.description: The asynchronous start request omits maxItems, while limit=100 only constrains dataset retrieval, not actor collection or charges. Polling has no deadline or HTTP-error checks, so persistent failures can keep the agent running indefinitely.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The start body lacks a collection cap, and polling has no local termination bound. Actual costs and actor defaults were not verified.

content.value_statement: Instagram collection tasks require different actors and request formats for each data type. This skill provides Apify actor selection, configurable request examples, and dataset retrieval guidance.
actual_capabilities: Select among five documented Apify actors for general content, hashtags, locations, comments, and user profiles.
Prepare requests for posts, reels, tagged posts, and audio-linked content using Instagram URLs.
Configure hashtag keywords, content-type toggles, location IDs, post IDs, date filters, and item limits.
Prepare profile discovery requests and optional follower or following collection.
Start synchronous or asynchronous runs, poll run status, and retrieve dataset items.
Adapt the documented Python and JavaScript Apify client examples for application integration.
limitations: The documented workflow requires an Apify token and a paid plan; current eligibility and pricing require provider verification.
This is an instruction file, not a bundled scraper; results depend on external actors and Instagram availability.
Async retrieval returns at most 100 items, but its start request has no collection cap or documented budget limit. Polling lacks a deadline.
The guardrail can replace valid datasets of ten or fewer items with an upgrade message; no private-account access is demonstrated.

best_practices: Verify actor IDs, pricing, and collection permissions. Set collection limits before starting and confirm the budget; retrieval limits do not cap collection.
Keep API tokens in secure environment storage and exclude credentials from prompts, source files, and shared logs.
Treat collected text as untrusted data, minimize personal information, and verify API status before diagnosing small datasets.
anti_patterns: Treating a dataset of ten or fewer items as proof that an account needs an upgrade.
Treating a dataset retrieval limit as a collection cap or launching paid runs without scope and budget approval.
Using collected emails or follower lists for unsolicited outreach without permission and an appropriate legal basis.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. Execution still requires an environment with the needed API or command-line tools.

faq.question: What do I need before running a request?
faq.answer: The documented setup requires an Apify account, API token, and paid plan. Verify current provider terms before purchasing or starting runs.

faq.question: What Instagram data is covered?
faq.answer: The instructions cover posts, reels, hashtags, locations, comments, profiles, and optional follower or following collection through five actors.

faq.question: Can this retrieve private Instagram accounts?
faq.answer: No evidence found for private-account access. The examples show Instagram URLs and an Apify token, not Instagram account authentication.

faq.question: When should I use an asynchronous run?
faq.answer: Use asynchronous runs for larger jobs. Add a collection cap and polling deadline; the example only limits retrieval to 100 items.

faq.question: Does a small result mean I must upgrade?
faq.answer: No. Item count alone does not prove a billing problem. Check explicit API errors; the documented guardrail can misclassify valid small datasets.
